answer: Each identity locks 70 in a dawn beacon pool, paying 20 to join. At dawn the beacon board lists the roster; each member posts a key-signed pulse proving it still holds its item, and auditors recompute its pulse chain. With two peers, one pays 90 once and recovers 70 after a clean epoch. Standalone, one pays a 50 premium, so one fake costs 140; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 70,000. Joint burn makes the kth fake cost 20 more to its cluster: one detected fake burns 70 plus 20 per peer, so 100 fakes lose 2,050 on one detection. A rented-cover ring fails on a pulse-key mismatch.
